name: Cross Hierarchical Control

cross_template_interactions.description: Thalamic gating provides multimodal input streams; hierarchical control generates predictions at each level of architectural hierarchy and propagates PE signals upward.
SN salience detection can occur at any hierarchy level; detected salience elevates that level's prediction error representation. Salience navigation across hierarchy levels.
Proactive/reactive control choice determines how hierarchy is navigated: proactive mode sustains current hierarchy level goal; reactive mode allows rapid hierarchy level switching in response to PE.
Spatial hierarchical control (room-floor-building) generates PE cascade. Temporal hierarchy operates in parallel (seconds-minutes-hours). Both feed into unified prediction error architecture.

Hierarchical predictions at different levels generate dose-response curves at different temporal scales. High-level (building-level) PE shows slow dose-response; low-level (room-level) PE shows fast response.
Hierarchical PE resolution determines attentional priority: high-PE hierarchy levels receive attentional focus. Hierarchy structure guides attention allocation across architectural features.
